answer: Requiring every agent identity to lock a refundable stake turns Sybil attacks into a budgeting problem. Each new identity must post its own bond, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand bonds, like buying a thousand walnuts one by one instead of one sack. The bond sits in escrow like a marble on a ledge: behave honestly and it rolls back to you, but proven misbehavior tips it off the ledge and it is slashed. An attacker can still buy identities, but the cost scales linearly with the number of fakes while the reward for any single fake stays small, so mass forgery stops paying for itself.
